newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Moscow says no details yet of bond issue.
newsitem.headline: Moscow says no details yet of bond issue.

text.p: Details of the volume and maturity of the City of Moscow's debut international bond will be fixed only when it is issued, a city official said on Wednesday.
Svetlana Lokhtina, head of the city government's financial department, also told Reuters no final decision had been taken on when the bond would be issued.
The city authorities earlier said CS First Boston and Nomura International had been selected as lead-manager for the issue -- Moscow's first such issue since before the 1917 Bolshevik revolution.
The city's press centre said the joint leads would be assisted by Russia's Alfa-Bank and Stolichny Bank Sberezhenii.
The offering would play an important role in implementing Moscow's investment programmes.
City officials had said in August that Moscow would issue foreign-currency bonds, probably for $300 million, on international markets.
Russia is also preparing a debut Eurobond issue and is currently awaiting an international rating.
Deputy Finance Minister Mikhail Kasyanov said on Friday that Russia hoped to issue its planned Eurobond late next month or early in November.
Russia has mandated JP Morgan and SBC Warburg to manage the issue. Market analysts have said the central government is likely to issue its bond before Moscow.
